items.title: Why the Form and Formless Realms Feel None of This

items.zh: 又色、無色界有情無有如是等苦，由彼有情非苦受器故。
items.en: Further, beings of the form and formless realms have none of these sufferings, because such beings are not vessels for painful feeling at all.

items.title: A Qualification: Even the Formless Have a Subtle Kind of Suffering

items.zh: 然由麁重苦故，說彼有苦。有煩惱故，有障礙故，於死及住不自在故。
items.en: Yet, because of the suffering of subtle underlying affliction, it is said that they too have suffering: because affliction is still present, because it still obstructs, and because they lack mastery over death and continued existence.

items.zh: 又無漏界中，一切麁重諸苦永斷。是故唯此是勝義樂，當知所餘一切是苦。
items.en: Further, in the uncontaminated realm alone, every subtle underlying affliction and its suffering are permanently eliminated. This alone, therefore, is ultimate happiness; everything else, it should be understood, is suffering.

items.title: Pleasure Mixed With Suffering, and Pleasure Without It

items.zh: 又於四種那落迦中無有樂受。如那落迦中，三種餓鬼中亦爾。
items.en: Further, in the four kinds of hells there is no pleasant feeling at all. As in the hells, so too among the three kinds of hungry ghosts.

items.zh: 諸大力鬼、傍生、人中，有外門所生資具樂可得，然為眾苦之所相雜。
items.en: Among powerful ghosts, animals, and humans, pleasure arising from external possessions can be found, yet it comes mixed together with a great deal of suffering.

items.zh: 又人趣中，轉輪王樂最勝微妙。由彼輪王出現世時，有成就七寶自然出現，故說彼王具足七寶。何等為七？所謂輪寶、象寶、馬寶、末尼珠寶、女寶、主藏臣寶、主兵臣寶。
items.en: Further, within the human destiny, the pleasure of a Wheel-Turning King is the most excellent and sublime of all. Because, when such a king appears in the world, seven treasures spontaneously appear together with him, that king is said to possess the seven treasures in full. What are these seven? The wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the wish-fulfilling-jewel treasure, the woman-treasure, the treasurer-minister treasure, and the general-minister treasure.

items.zh: 爾時輪寶等現，其相云何？七寶現相，如經廣說。
若彼輪王王四洲者，一切小王望風順化，各自白言：某城邑聚落，天之所有，唯願大王垂恩教勅，我等皆當為天僕隸。爾時輪王便即勅令：汝等諸王！各於自境以理獎化，當以如法，勿以非法。又復汝等於國於家勿行非法行，勿行不平等行。
items.en: If that Wheel-Turning King rules all four continents, every lesser king, sensing his influence from afar, submits and is transformed by it of his own accord. At that time, the Wheel-Turning King issues this command: "You kings, each govern your own domain according to what is right, encouraging and transforming your people in accordance with the Dharma, never contrary to it. Further, in your own state and household, engage in no unlawful conduct, no conduct that treats others unfairly."

items.zh: 若彼輪王王三洲者，先遣使往，然後從化。若彼輪王王二洲者，興師現威，後乃從化。若彼輪王王一洲者，便自往彼，奮戈揮刃，然後從化。
items.en: If that Wheel-Turning King rules three continents, he first sends envoys, and only then do the lesser kings submit to his transformation. If he rules two continents, he must raise an army and display his might, and only then do they submit. If he rules a single continent, he must go there in person, brandishing weapons, and only then do they submit.

items.title: The Desire-Realm Heavens' Palaces and Wish-Fulfilling Trees

items.zh: 復次，諸天受其廣大天之富樂。形色殊妙，多諸適悅，於自宮中而得久住。其身內外皆悉清潔，無有臭穢。又人身內多有不淨，所謂塵垢筋骨脾腎心肝；彼皆無有。
items.en: Further, the gods enjoy the vast wealth and pleasure proper to a god: their form and colouring are supremely fine, they meet with pleasing circumstances at every turn, and they dwell for a long time in their own heavenly palaces. Their bodies, inside and out, are entirely clean, free of any foulness — for a human body contains a great deal of impurity, dust and grime, sinew and bone, spleen and kidney, heart and liver, none of which the gods possess at all.

items.zh: 又彼諸天有四種宮殿，所謂金、銀、頗胝、琉璃所成，種種文綵綺飾莊嚴。
items.en: Further, these gods have four kinds of palace, made of gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli, adorned throughout with every kind of ornamental pattern and decoration.

items.zh: 種種臺閣、種種樓觀、種種層級、種種窓牖、種種羅網，皆可愛樂。種種末尼以為綺鈿，周匝放光，共相照曜。
復有食樹，從其樹裏出四食味，名曰蘇陀，所謂青黃赤白。復有飲樹，從此流出甘美之飲。復有乘樹，從此出生種種妙乘，所謂車輅輦輿等。復有衣樹，從此出生種種妙衣，其衣細軟，妙色鮮潔，雜綵間飾。復有莊嚴具樹，從此出生種種微妙莊嚴之具，所謂末尼、臂印、耳璫、環釧，及以手足綺飾之具。如是等類諸莊嚴具，皆以種種妙末尼寶而間飾之。復有熏香鬘樹，從此出生種種塗香、種種熏香、種種花鬘。
items.en: There is, further, a food-tree, which produces from within itself four flavours of food called sudhā — blue, yellow, red, and white. There is a drink-tree, from which flows a sweet and delicious beverage. There is a vehicle-tree, which produces every kind of wondrous conveyance. There is a garment-tree, which produces every kind of wondrous clothing. There is an ornament-tree, which produces every kind of wondrous adornment. There is an incense-and-garland tree, which produces every kind of scented paste, every kind of incense, and every kind of flower garland.

items.zh: 復有大集會樹，最勝微妙。其根深固五十踰繕那，其身高挺百踰繕那，枝條及葉遍覆八十踰繕那；雜花開發，其香順風熏百踰繕那，逆風熏五十踰繕那。於此樹下，三十三天雨四月中，以天妙五欲共相娛樂。
items.en: There is, further, the Tree of the Great Assembly, most excellent and sublime of all — its roots sunk fifty yojanas deep, its trunk rising a hundred yojanas tall, its branches and leaves spreading to cover eighty yojanas; when its manifold blossoms open, their fragrance carries a hundred yojanas downwind and fifty yojanas upwind. Beneath this very tree, the Thirty-Three spend the four months of the rainy season, delighting together in the heavenly pleasures of the five senses.

items.title: More Wish-Trees, and How Heavenly Enjoyment Actually Works

items.zh: 復有歌笑舞樂之樹，從此出生歌笑舞等種種樂器。又有資具之樹，從此出生種種資具，所謂食飲之具、坐臥之具、如是等類種種資具。
items.en: There is, further, a tree of song, laughter, dance, and music, which produces every kind of instrument for song, laughter, dance, and the rest. There is, further, a tree of provisions, which produces every kind of provision — implements for food and drink, for sitting and lying down, and every other such thing.

items.zh: 又彼諸天欲受用時，隨欲隨業，應其所須，來現手中。
items.en: Further, whenever these gods wish to make use of something, according to their wish and according to their karma, whatever they need simply appears, already in hand.

items.title: Asuras' Palaces, and Uttarakuru's Wish-Fulfilling Paradise

items.zh: 又諸非天，隨其所應，受用種種宮殿富樂應知。
items.en: Further, it should be understood that the asuras, according to what befits them, likewise enjoy various palaces and heavenly wealth.

items.zh: 又北拘盧洲有如是相樹，名曰如意。彼諸人眾所欲資具，從樹而取。不由思惟，隨其所須，自然在手。復有秔稻，不種而穫。無有我所。
items.en: Further, in Uttarakuru there is a tree of just this kind, called the Wish-Fulfilling Tree. Whatever provisions its people desire, they take from this tree — with no need even to think about it, whatever is needed simply appears, of itself, already in hand. There is, further, rice that ripens and is harvested without ever being sown. Nothing there is held as "mine."

items.zh: 又彼有情竟無繫屬、決定勝進。
items.en: Further, the beings there are entirely without bonds of attachment, yet also without any decisive path to what is truly excellent.

blocks.text: Today the treatise answers a question raised by everything since Day 25: is any existence free of suffering? The answer is precise and important. Then it turns to pleasure, describing the best pleasures available in the desire realm: those of a wheel-turning king, the desire heavens, and the paradise of Uttarakuru. Read the description of pleasure in the light of the answer about suffering.

Two passages are untranslated: 0298a11 ("What do the wheel-treasure and the rest look like when they appear? The appearance of the seven treasures is as explained at length in the sūtras") and 0298a27–a29 (the gods' palaces have every kind of terrace, tower, storey, window, and lattice, set with jewels that light one another).

Beings of the form and formless realms do not suffer any of the pains described so far, "because such beings are not vessels for painful feeling at all". Venerable Miào Jìng: their karmic result cannot hold pain.

Yet they still suffer, "because of coarse burden" (麁重, Day 7). Venerable Miào Jìng: coarse burden here is "chiefly the seeds of affliction"; enjoying meditative bliss, "the mind still harbours attachment, views, and conceit". They also lack mastery over death and continued existence. Master Cháng Bǎi: they have not left the three realms and may fall into any destiny after death.

"This alone is ultimate happiness; everything else, it should be understood, is suffering": only the **uncontaminated realm** (無漏界). Master Cháng Bǎi: this belongs to those in whom every subtle affliction is cut, arhats and Buddhas; stream-enterers and first-stage bodhisattvas, not yet complete, still have subtle suffering.
This sentence is the key to the whole survey of the realms. The point of describing pleasure and pain in such detail is to show that no conditioned existence, however refined, is a refuge.

There is no pleasant feeling at all in the four kinds of hell or among the three kinds of ghost. Powerful ghosts, animals, and humans have pleasure from external possessions, but mixed with much suffering. The best human pleasure is that of the **wheel-turning king** (Day 14), with his seven treasures: wheel, elephant, horse, jewel, queen, treasurer, and general. Master Cháng Bǎi adds, citing the *Abhidharmakośa*, that no wheel-turning king kills; a king of one continent who must "brandish weapons" only makes a show of force.
A king of four continents commands lesser kings to "govern rightly by the Dharma". The ideal ruler in this treatise is a moral teacher.

The gods' bodies are clean inside and out, with no organs. Their palaces are of gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli. Trees supply their every need: a food-tree yields nectar (*sudhā*) in four colours, which, Master Cháng Bǎi notes, is why the asuras war with them. Under the great tree of the Thirty-Three they enjoy themselves through the four months of the rainy season. What they wish for appears "according to their wish and according to their karma". Master Cháng Bǎi: "gods' enjoyment is not without limit"; it varies with merit, as on Day 28.

On the northern continent a wish-fulfilling tree supplies everything "with no need even to think about it"; rice ripens unsown; nothing is held as "mine". Yet its people are "without bonds of attachment, yet also without any decisive path". The *Pīxún jì*, cited by Master Cháng Bǎi: they have no parents, spouses, or possessions to cling to, but also no mindfulness or cutting of afflictions, so "noble ones are never born there". A perfect society without the path is still not liberation. Uttarakuru is listed among the unfavourable conditions for practice for exactly this reason.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why do beings of the form and formless realms lack those sufferings?
options: because they are "not vessels for painful feeling" — their karmic result cannot hold painful feeling
quiz.why: "Beings of the form and formless realms have none of these sufferings, because such beings are not vessels for painful feeling at all." Venerable Miào Jìng: "their karmic result is not a vessel that can hold suffering." A is wrong: they are still within the three realms, and the next section says they have subtle suffering.

quiz.q: The text says the upper realms "have suffering because of 麤重," rendered "the suffering of subtle underlying affliction." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 麤重?
options: chiefly the seeds of affliction — enjoying meditative bliss in heaven, the mind still holds attachment, views, and conceit
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "麤重 … chiefly the seeds of affliction — that is suffering"; "in heaven they enjoy meditative bliss, yet the mind still harbours attachment, views, and conceit." The rendering "subtle underlying affliction" captures the latent, seed-like sense; though the characters literally mean "coarse and heavy," they denote an underlying unwieldiness. A reads the characters too literally.

quiz.q: The text says only the uncontaminated realm "is ultimate happiness; everything else … is suffering." According to Master Cháng Bǎi, who has this ultimate happiness?
options: beings at the peak of existence
those of the complete uncontaminated realm, such as arhats or buddhas; stream-enterers and first-ground bodhisattvas, not yet complete, still have subtle suffering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The complete uncontaminated realm — arhats or buddhas — in whom all subtle afflictions of attachment and views, even those of the cognitive obscuration, are permanently cut: that is ultimate happiness … those not yet complete, such as stream-enterers or first-ground bodhisattvas, still have subtle suffering." Venerable Miào Jìng: "one must reach arhatship to transcend the three realms." D is §38's highest human pleasure, still contaminated.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, where is there no pleasant feeling at all, and where is pleasure mixed with suffering?
options: none in heaven; some in hell
none among humans; some among ghosts
none in the four kinds of hell or the three kinds of ghost; powerful ghosts, animals, and humans have pleasure from external possessions, but mixed with much suffering
quiz.why: "In the four kinds of hells there is no pleasant feeling at all. As in the hells, so too among the three kinds of hungry ghosts. Among powerful ghosts, animals, and humans, pleasure arising from external possessions can be found, yet it comes mixed together with a great deal of suffering." Master Cháng Bǎi: powerful ghosts are wealthy ones; the mixed-in pain includes having too much or too little, and the pain of pursuit.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of the Wheel-Turning King's seven treasures?
quiz.why: The seven: wheel, elephant, horse, wish-fulfilling jewel, woman, treasurer-minister, and general-minister. The wish-fulfilling tree is §42's tree in Uttarakuru. Master Cháng Bǎi: the treasurer knows where treasure lies in the earth and brings it out for the king; the general is an invincible commander.

quiz.q: The text says what the gods want appears in hand "according to their wish and according to their karma." According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what does "according to their karma" remind us?
options: heavenly enjoyment is not unlimited — what reaches the hand differs in refinement according to karma and merit
karma does not operate in heaven
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Gods' enjoyment is not without limit; according to the size of their karma and merit, what comes to hand differs in refinement — a single thought, and the tree supplies their every need." C and D are the opposite: even wish-fulfilment has a karmic ceiling — which echoes the suffering of being scorned in §34.

quiz.q: The text says Uttarakuru's beings are "without bonds, and without the decisive path," rendered "without bonds of attachment, yet also without any decisive path." How does Master Cháng Bǎi (citing the Pixunji) explain it?
options: no bonds: no parents, spouses, servants, or other attachments; no decisive path: no mindfulness, awareness, or cutting of afflictions — only higher rebirth, and noble ones are never born there
they will surely fall into hell
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "Having no objects of attachment is called being without bonds … lacking mindfulness, awareness, and the realised cutting of afflictions is called lacking the decisive path. Hence noble ones are never reborn there." Master Cháng Bǎi: they were born there through the ten wholesome deeds and will be reborn in heaven — higher rebirth — "but without the noble path's decisive excellence"; Uttarakuru is one of the eight unfavorable conditions. "Decisive path" corresponds to liberation, as opposed to mere higher rebirth.
